name: Hilti-Oxford Dataset
description: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) is being deployed in real-world applications, however many state-of-the-art solutions still struggle in many common scenarios. A key necessity in progressing SLAM research is the availability of high-quality datasets and fair and transparent benchmarking. To this end, we have created the Hilti-Oxford Dataset, to push state-of-the-art SLAM systems to their limits. The dataset has a variety of challenges ranging from sparse and regular construction sites to a 17th century neoclassical building with fine details and curved surfaces. To encourage multi-modal SLAM approaches, we designed a data collection platform featuring a lidar, five cameras, and an IMU (Inertial Measurement Unit). With the goal of benchmarking SLAM algorithms for tasks where accuracy and robustness are paramount, we implemented a novel ground truth collection method that enables our dataset to accurately measure SLAM pose errors with millimeter accuracy. evaluation_method: trajectory/pose error scoring against ground truth
typical_sota_score: varies by metric; state-of-the-art SLAM methods report median translation errors roughly in the ~10–100 mm range and rotation errors in the ~0.1–1° range on the most challenging sequences, depending on modality and sequence difficulty
reputation: Widely regarded as a strong real-world SLAM benchmark because it provides challenging scenes and millimeter-accurate ground truth.
notes: Non-LLM robotics benchmark; challenging real-world dataset with multimodal sensing and high-precision ground truth, so results are not directly comparable to synthetic SLAM benchmarks.
